v1.feedback: The apricity concept genuinely drives palette, lighting, and motion — the low-sun raking angle and frost-stiffening of coral undulation are well-chosen. However, the underlying coral forms are built from unmodified cylinder/box/sphere primitives with only minor vertex displacement, so they read as blocky stacks rather than organic reef structure; consider fractal branching or recursive L-system placement to earn the coral silhouette. The crystal-facet effect (step function on y) looks like aliasing rather than intentional faceting — try quantizing normals or introducing actual sharp-edge geometry. The uApricity ramp saturates at 8s and the piece becomes essentially static after that; a slow seasonal breathe oscillating between 0.7–1.0 would keep the sun-warmth feeling alive without undoing the morph.

v2.feedback: The apricity concept lands in the uniforms (frost-stiffness relaxation, low raking sun, cold-to-warm color cycle) but 45 colonies scattered across radius 16 at only 2–3 branching levels will read as sparse sticks on a dark plane, not a reef — tighten the placement radius to ~6–8 and push maxDepth to 4 so the canopy fills the frame. The faceted-normal quantization is a nice touch but the flat substrate plane undercuts it; replace the plane with a subtle displacement mesh or remove it entirely. The sinusoidal apricity cycle is too predictable — use a slow asymmetric ramp (long cold, brief warm peak) so the warmth feels earned, like actual winter sun breaking through.
